issue.title: Count D 55 and D 61 at M 64, kf 23, and test the M 40 and M 48 zeros there

labels.name: mac
labels.description: Task for mac, the coordinator's M5 Mac

issue.body:
**What.** The third-resolution counts at M 64, kf 23, at D 61.03 (on `I141-mac/states/modecount_state_D61.0264_M64_kf23.npz`, ks 191) and at D 55.04 (setup builds the fitted layout). Before each count, check that det M changes sign across λ_phys and that the two LUs agree to 1e-4. Then put circles on the M 64 state at the M 48 positions (#230 at D 61, #238 at D 55) and the M 40 ones (#231). Recommended in #141's summary (its task 3), with D 55 added.

**Why.** At D 55 the M 48 extras are absent at M 40, which has others (#231). A fourth resolution, above M 48, shows whether any extra zero keeps its λ.

**Acceptance (can fail).** Each count's 8 box windings with both mismatch counts. Each circle's winding with the λ_phys control. Each M 48 and M 40 zero present or absent at M 64.

**Depends on.** #141, #231.

The det check at λ_phys ∓ 0.015 found a sign change in both LUs, with the LUs 5.3e-7 and 1.2e-7 apart and pivots 7.9e-13 … 6.4e5.

**The control circles** (R 0.2, n0 20, criterion: winding +1 with the zero within 1e-5 of λ_phys):

| D | winding | max step | mismatches | zero located | from λ_phys | circle's estimate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 61.03 | +1 | 0.342 rad | 0 | 2.043995 − 0.000281i | **5.4e-4** | 1.1e-3 |
| 55.04 | +1 | 0.334 rad | 0 | 2.047662 − 0.000005i | **2.3e-5** | 1.4e-5 |
| 55.04 at M 48 (#238), for comparison | +1 | 0.332 rad | 0 | 2.047684 | 5e-8 | 4.0e-8 |
| 55.04 at M 40 (#231), for comparison | +1 | 0.338 rad | 0 | 2.047684 | 3e-8 | 4.6e-8 |

The windings are clean. The positions are not. A real zero must come out real, and at D 61 the circle puts it 2.8e-4 off the axis.

**Spectrum of ln h on each circle** (`scripts/circle_spectrum.py`, from the cache, no new determinants). After dividing out the zero and the local trend, ln h is analytic on and outside the disc up to the nearest other singularity, so its Fourier coefficients a_k on the 20 base points should fall geometrically for k > 0 and vanish for k < −1. Instead they fall to a **white floor at every |k|**:

| circle | a_1 | a_2 | a_3 | floor (k ≥ 4 and all k ≤ −2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D 61, M 64 | 0.79 | 3.1e-2 | 7.8e-4 | **3e-3 … 9e-3** |
| D 55, M 64 | 0.79 | 3.2e-2 | 1.9e-3 | **3e-5 … 1.6e-4** |
| D 55, M 48 (#238) | | | | about 3e-7 |
| D 55, M 40 (#231) | | | | about 1e-7 |

A floor ε in a₋₁ moves the located zero by about Rε, which is 2e-5 at D 55 and up to 1e-3 at D 61, as observed. So the M 64 complex determinant carries an error that is not smooth in λ. It is about 2e-2 per point at D 61 and 4e-4 at D 55 in ln det, against about 1e-6 at M 48. The windings are not affected, since 2e-2 rad is far below the 0.34 rad steps. But the error is 10³–10⁵ times larger than the LU disagreement at real λ (1e-5 at D 61, 5e-7 at D 55), so it is not plain LU rounding.

The 1e-5 criterion is not loosened, and the position circles do not run until the cause is known (coordinator). Running now: a smoothness probe (`scripts/smooth_probe.py`, criteria in `I252-mac/README.md` before the runs). It measures (A) the change of ln|det| from x0 to x0 + 1e-9i, which isolates the switch to the complex horizon solves, and (B) a second difference at δ = 1e-7 on a circle point. It runs on D 61 M 64, D 55 M 64, and the D 61 M 48 state as the control that must come out smooth.

cpu: load about 7 on 10 cores, 2 single-thread processes of mine at about 0.1 GB each. Memory: 77% free reported, swap 8.4 of 9.2 GB used.

**Probe verdict and cause** (mac, 18:30 UTC). The M 64 complex determinant carries a non-smooth error. It enters through the matrix entries of the two series blocks, not through the complex path or the LU. The mode matrix is near-singular, which turns that entry error into the 1e-4 to 1e-2 noise in ln det. The position circles and the counts stay held.

**1. Smoothness probe** (`scripts/smooth_probe.py`). It compares ln det at x0 and x0 + 1e-9i (A), and takes the second difference at δ = 1e-7 on a circle point (B). The criterion was 1e-6 for both.

| state | A | B |
|---|---|---|
| D 61, M 48, ks 127 (control) | 9.5e-7 | **3.6e-5** |
| D 55, M 64, ks 150 | 2.7e-4 | 8.6e-4 |
| D 61, M 64, ks 191 | 1.7e-2 | 1.7e-2 |

**The control fails its B criterion, so by the rule written first the probe is not read as pass or fail.** M 48 has the same kind of error, 500 times smaller. The numbers above are measurements.

**2. Where it enters.** Each test's reading was written before its run.

| test | D 61, M 48 | D 55, M 64 | D 61, M 64 |
|---|---|---|---|
| mode matrix analytic across the axis: \|M(x0+iε) − M(x0) − i(M(x0+ε) − M(x0))\| / \|M(x0+ε) − M(x0)\|, ε 1e-9 | 8e-8 (the ε² term) | 8e-8 | |
| non-smooth error of the entries, max \|second difference\| / max \|entry\| at steps 2^-40 and 2^-46 (equal at both, so not curvature): centre-series block | 3e-25 | **3e-19** | **5e-20** |
| the same, Taylor segments | ≤ 2e-28 | ≤ 2e-28 | ≤ 2e-28 |
| the same, horizon-series block | 3e-24 | **5e-22** | **2e-21** |
| the same at D 61, M 64 with ks 100 or 127 instead of 191 | | | identical to 3 digits |
| LU of Mᵀ against M (the same det), Δ ln det | 25 | 6.6 | 35 |
| M with random 1e-30 relative entry perturbations, Δ ln det | 5e-5 … 6e-4 | 2e-5 … 4e-5 | 5e-4 … 8e-4 |
| exact power-of-two row and column equilibration, then 1e-30 perturbations | | 4e-2 … 7e-2 (worse) | |

What the table shows:

- **The complex path is not at fault.** The matrix built at x0 + 1e-9i is analytic in its entries to the size of the ε² term. A moves ln det by the full noise only because any change of λ reshuffles the rounding.
- **The LU is not at fault either.** Its result depends on the rounding path: transposing changes ln det by 6.6 to 35, at M 48 as at M 64. A relative 1e-30 change of the entries moves ln det by up to 8e-4. So σ_min/σ_max of the mode matrix is about 1e-26 at both M, which is close to the double-double limit (1.2e-32). Equilibration makes it worse, so this is the matrix's conditioning and not the LU's scaling.
- **What changes from M 48 to M 64 is the accuracy of the entries in the two series blocks.** The centre-series rows (x = 0 to 0.3) lose 5 to 6 more digits, and the horizon-series rows (u = 0 to 0.3) lose 2 to 3 more. The Taylor segments stay at double-double rounding. The horizon order (ks 100, 127, 191) changes nothing. Both series take one d/dτ per order (#141). My reading, not tested: the tangent's terms grow with M before they decay, so their double-double sums lose those digits, while the background's own series still converges cleanly (|F| 1e-20).
- **The noise tracks the horizon block.** The ratio of ln det noise to horizon-block entry error is about 1e19 at all three states, within 5×. The centre block's error does not track it.

**What it does to the results.** The windings are unaffected, since 2e-2 rad of noise is far below the π/4 tolerance and the halves-sum check is exact arithmetic. Positions are good to about Rε: 5e-4 to 1e-3 at D 61 and 2e-5 at D 55. That is what the λ_phys circles showed, and it is 10 to 500 times finer than the 0.01 \"keeps its λ\" criterion. The real-axis determinant check (two LUs within 1e-4) cannot see this, because both LUs factor the same matrix. At M 48 the noise (about 3.6e-5) is harmless for every count and position so far.

**What a fix would take** (the coordinator decides):
- (a) More precision in the two series of the tangent, for example quad-double accumulation in `modecount_cx`'s `centre_series_c` and `horizon_series_c`. That is a modecount_cx change and its rebuild (about 1 min), with hp itself untouched, and probably a day's work. The fix is confirmed if matrix_noise's series rows fall to about 1e-28 and the λ_phys circle locates λ_phys to 1e-7.
- (b) Shorter series spans. A node at 0.15 shortens the centre series (#141's D 30 layout), but the noise tracks the horizon block, and a node at 0.85 made det M unusable at D 61 (#141). A test at D 55: setup with a 0.15 node, then matrix_noise, then the λ_phys circle, about 1.5 h.
- (c) Restate the λ_phys gate against the measured floor, for example the zero within 3 times the circle's own estimate and within 1e-3, and run the circles now. That is about 8 h on 2 slots. It answers the question at a resolution of about 1e-3, enough for the 0.01 criterion. It is not done here, since a fired control may not be loosened without your decision.

## Closing summary (mac, 23:58 UTC), ended early on the coordinator's word

**All 8 M 48 zero positions are absent at M 64, and so are the 3 M 40 positions tested.** None of the 11 positions looked for keeps its λ. The full M 64 counts were held (coordinator) and did not run. The D 61 M 40 circle at 1.98 + 1.20i was killed part-way at the coordinator's request.

**Setups and determinant checks** (sign change across λ_phys in both LUs, the LUs within 1e-4):
- D 61, M 64, kf 23 (#141's state, ks 191, |F| 8.5e-21): pass, LUs 9.3e-6 and 1.2e-5 apart.
- Its control, the node-0.85 state: fails as required, LUs 0.84 and 1.11 apart, opposite signs.
- D 55, M 64, kf 23: new setup from the M 48 state (ks 100 → 150, |F| 1.4e-7 → 2.1e-20, 1485 s): pass, LUs 5e-7 and 1e-7 apart.

**λ_phys controls.** Both circles wind +1 with max step 0.34 rad. The **original gate (zero within 1e-5) fired at both D**: D 61 was 5.4e-4 off and D 55 2.3e-5 off. The cause is measured (posted above): the series blocks of the M 64 mode matrix carry non-smooth entry error, and the near-singular matrix turns it into ln det noise of 1.7e-2 at D 61 and 8.6e-4 at D 55. Windings are unaffected. Under the **restated gate** (option (c): winds +1, zero within 3× the circle's own estimate and within 1e-3 of λ_phys) both pass: 5.4e-4 against a limit of 1e-3 at D 61, and 2.3e-5 against 4.1e-5 at D 55.

**Reading.** Combined with #231 (the D 55 M 48 zeros absent at M 40, and M 40 having its own), every extra zero located so far at D 55 and D 61 vanishes when the resolution changes. That is the behaviour of a truncation artifact. A mode would keep its λ. The limits: these are discs of radius 0.2–0.3 around the old positions, not counts, so M 64 may have extra zeros elsewhere, and 8 of the M 40 positions were not tested.

Code: `wip/i252` (main 590d88a with #242's rule; no code changes of mine).

### Discrepancies
1. The original λ_phys gate (1e-5) fired at both D at M 64. Its cause is measured: series-block entry error at M 64 on a near-singular mode matrix (σ_min/σ_max about 1e-26).
2. The smoothness probe's own M 48 control failed its 1e-6 criterion (3.6e-5), so the probe is read only as measurements.
3. The real-axis determinant check cannot see this noise, because both LUs factor the same matrix (relevant to #253).

### Recommended tasks
